item.title: Boston Scientific Exposes 117,000 Records Following Voice Phishing Attack
item.description:
Boston Scientific Exposes 117,000 Records Following Voice Phishing Attack

Boston Scientific, a Massachusetts-based medical device manufacturer, is sending data breach notices to individuals after a cyberattack exposed personal and medical information belonging to 117,789 people in the United States. The incident marks the second cybersecurity event for the company this year.

🔍 Overview

The attack exposed cloud-based applications and cloud-hosted data between May 7 and May 1, 2025. Boston Scientific became aware of the unauthorized access on May 12. A subsequent investigation determined that a data breach occurred on November 5. The exposed information included personal details and medical information for individuals in multiple U.S. states.

🧩 How it works

According to notification samples shared with U.S. authorities, the hacker gained access to the company’s cloud infrastructure using social engineering in a voice phishing (vishing) attack.

⚙️ Key details

  • Data Exposed: Personal details and medical information.
  • Data Not Exposed: The notification specifies that patient medical records, data from remote monitoring systems, connected medical devices, and clinical case management or workflow applications were not exposed.
  • Scope: The incident impacted 117,789 individuals according to the Texas Attorney General breach portal.
  • Business Impact: The company stated there was no disruption to manufacturing, ordering, distribution, or service to patients and healthcare providers, and no impact on operations, performance, remote monitoring, or the safety of its products.

📊 Incident Comparison

This breach is distinct from a previous cyberattack disclosed on August 25, which caused network outages and global operational disruptions. A Boston Scientific spokesperson confirmed the most recent incident is unrelated to the August 2026 intrusion; a CrowdStrike investigation into that earlier attack found no evidence that attackers compromised cloud applications.

💡 Why it matters

As one of the world’s largest medical device manufacturers with more than 59,000 employees, 13 manufacturing facilities, and a presence in 127 countries, Boston Scientific’s data security is critical. The company contained the incident, investigated with outside cybersecurity experts, and notified law enforcement. However, the company is not offering free credit monitoring and instead recommends impacted individuals use free credit reports, place fraud alerts, and consider credit freezes.

#databreach #cybersecurity #medicaldevices #vishing #BostonScientific

Source: New Boston Scientific data breach exposes personal, medical info

item.title: pCloud Pass users report unauthorized device connections following cyberattack
item.description:
pCloud Pass users report unauthorized device connections following cyberattack

The pCloud Pass password manager was recently targeted by a cyberattack, resulting in users reporting that unknown devices had connected to their accounts, some with two-factor authentication (2FA) enabled. The attack was contained by the pCloud team, though a small number of user email addresses were exposed.

🔍 Overview

According to pCloud, a cyberattack targeting pCloud Pass occurred and was promptly contained. The company stated that a small number of pCloud Pass user email addresses were exposed and that login attempts were made. The system automatically sent notifications to each of these affected addresses.

⚙️ Key details

  • Users reported receiving notifications warning that an unfamiliar device named “pd” connected to their account from IP address 45.131.244.7 in Luxembourg.
  • The IP address is reportedly part of pCloud’s own infrastructure.
  • Notifications were received by customers who had 2FA enabled.
  • Some users who never used the password manager, including those with deleted storage accounts, also received the alerts.
  • PCloud stated the attack was isolated to the password manager, and cloud storage services were not affected.
  • Passwords, notes, and other information stored in pCloud Pass are encrypted on customer devices and were not compromised.
  • It is unknown whether encrypted password vaults were accessed or stolen during the attack.
  • A reader noted that the “Open settings” link in the email notifications pointed to passqa1.pcloud.com, a QA environment, rather than the production site.

💡 Why it matters

Threat actors who obtain encrypted password vaults can attempt to crack them offline, bypassing the service’s login rate limits and two-factor authentication protections. This risk was demonstrated in the 2022 LastPass breach, where stolen encrypted password vaults were linked to cryptocurrency thefts after attackers cracked weak or reused master passwords.

🛡️ Security advice

  • pCloud is warning customers to watch for phishing attacks.
  • The company states it will never ask for master passwords or recovery words over email, phone, or chat.
  • PCloud noted that advancements in artificial intelligence are accelerating the discovery of software vulnerabilities, though it did not state that this specific attack was AI-powered.

#pCloud #PasswordManager #Cybersecurity #DataBreach #2FA

Source: pCloud confirms password manager hack after suspicious login alerts

item.title: SAP Confirms Cyberattack Involving Source Code Modification
item.description:
SAP Confirms Cyberattack Involving Source Code Modification

SAP has confirmed taking urgent action to protect its customers after detecting suspicious activity in its IT environment, a cyberattack the company tracks under the code name “Project Granite.”

🏢 Company Profile

SAP is one of the world’s largest enterprise software vendors, based in Walddorf, Germany. Key operational details include:

  • Employees: 110,000 across 157 countries
  • Subscribers: 300 million
  • Annual Revenue: Over $40 billion

🔍 Incident Details

According to reports from Der Spiegel, which accessed an internal SAP memo, the attackers breached SAP’s GitHub environment, potentially with the aid of AI tools. Insider sources indicated that authentications tokens were stolen from SAP employees and used to copy and modify source code on GitHub.

Aspect Detail
Internal Code Name Project Granite
Breach Vector GitHub environment
Suspected Aid AI tools
Actions Taken by Attacker Stole authentication tokens; copied and modified source code

🛡️ Offical Response

SAP stated that it prompted all employees to keep project details confidential and implemented necessary measures to preserve service security. A company representative told BleepingComputer:

“SAP has identified suspicious activity and promptly implemented the necessary measures to protect its customers and preserve the security of its services.”

Regarding the scope of the compromise, SAP noted:

“Based on our investigation to date, we have found no evidence of unauthorized access to customer business data.”

“Our customers trust us to protect their data, and that remains our highest priority. In a highly dynamic threat environment, we will continue to strengthen our security to provide the secure and resilient environment our customers depend on.”

Despite this, SAP has not specified which environments were observed having suspicious activity, nor has it advised customers downloading code or performing updates from specific repositories to take action. A spokesperson declined to share further information on this matter.

☣️ Context

The incident follows a public warning from Germany’s Federal Office for Information Security (BSI) regarding agentic AI tools that empower cyberattacks, such as ARTEX, CAIRN, and PentAGI. This follows reports from Swiss and Italian national cybersecurity agencies regarding the first detections of large-scale AI-driven cyberattacks targeting critical infrastructure.

#SAP #Cybersecurity #DataBreach #AIsecurity

Source: SAP confirms security incident after suspicious GitHub activity

item.title: 1Password discloses breach after GitHub account compromise
item.description:
1Password discloses breach after GitHub account compromise

1Password disclosed a data breach after an employee’s corporate GitHub account was hacked. The attacker used the compromised account to deploy malicious code to the company’s backend services to steal customer data.

🔍 Overview

The company began investigating the breach on November 19 after detecting indications that an employee’s GitHub account had been compromised. 1Password states that customer password vaults and the encryption keys protecting them were not compromised in the attack.

🧩 How it works

The attacker accessed private source code repositories and injected malicious code into backend services that downloaded customer account records. The malicious code also stole internal company source code and accessed the company’s continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) environment, potentially exposing internal infrastructure credentials.

⚙️ Key details

The following customer data was stolen in the breach:

  • Customer names and email addresses
  • Account and user IDs
  • Account creation and last sign-in timestamps
  • Public cryptographic keys
  • Secure Remote Password (SRP) protocol parameters
  • Invitation, provisioning, and account recovery tokens
  • Other internal account metadata

The stolen tokens were embedded in links that 1Password emailed to users to accept account provisioning invitations or recover their accounts. 1Password says these tokens cannot be used on their own to access customer accounts, as completing the invitation or recovery process requires either single sign-on (SSO) authentication or a six-digit verification code sent to the user’s registered email address.

🚀 Availability

1Password has disabled the compromised GitHub account, revoked the stolen token, restored clean versions of affected services, and rotated or revoked potentially exposed infrastructure credentials. The company has also hired independent cybersecurity experts to validate its remediation efforts. As a precaution against brute-force attacks, 1Password has strengthened these verification codes from six numeric digits to ten alphanumeric characters. The company states that only a small number of users were affected and have been individually notified.

💡 Why it matters

While customer vaults were not compromised, the stolen data is valuable to threat actors as it provides a list of known 1Password users who could be targeted in phishing campaigns. Threat actors could send emails impersonating 1Password, using the breach as a lure to trick customers into disclosing their account passwords, Secret Keys, or recovery verification codes. 1Password is not requiring customers to change their account passwords or Secret Keys but warns them to watch for unexpected invitations, account recovery requests, and other potential phishing attempts.

#1Password #DataBreach #CyberSecurity #GitHub #Phishing

Source: 1Password customer data stolen after employee GitHub account breach

item.title: CIA and FinCEN Report Cyberattacks Using ARTEX Framework
item.description:
CIA and FinCEN Report Cyberattacks Using ARTEX Framework

Unknown attackers breached an open-source intelligence (OSINT) analysis system at the US Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) and also affected the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI) and the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency. Additionally, the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) disclosed an investigation into unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems.

🔍 Overview

  • The cyberattack was reportedly carried out using the ARTEX AI-powered penetration testing framework.
  • The incident affected the CIA, the ODNI, and the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency.
  • FinCEN is a US Department of the Treasury bureau that acts as the country’s official Financial Intelligence Unit and protects the nation’s financial system from illicit activities.

⚙️ Key details

  • The CIA and ODNI have not yet replied to a request for more details regarding the incident.
  • No classified data or systems were exposed in the breach.
  • A source stated, “The hack did not involve our classified networks or classified information, and no other systems are currently at risk.”
  • After detecting the attack, FinCEN took some systems offline as a precaution and told banks to use the Financial Institutions Hotline to file reports, since some services may be unavailable.
  • It is unclear how the attackers gained access, when the breach occurred, or whether they stole any information from the compromised systems.

💡 Why it matters

  • These incidents follow a series of other cyberattacks that have led to security breaches at other US federal agencies in recent years.
  • One week ago, the US National Security Agency’s classified network suffered a days-long outage, which the agency attributed to scheduled routine maintenance.
  • Two years ago, the Silk Typhoon Chinese state-backed hacking group breached the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), the Treasury’s Office of Financial Research, and the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States.
  • Hackers reportedly breached the FBI’s National Crime Information Center (NCIC).
  • The ShinyHunters extortion group claimed it breached the FBI’s recruitment website, FBIJobs.gov, prompting an FBI investigation that led to the arrests of multiple suspected members.

#cybersecurity #CIA #FinCEN #AI #databreach

Source: Hackers reportedly breached CIA intelligence analysis system

item.title: Exposed API Leads to Customer Credential Exposure at Radware
item.description:
Exposed API Leads to Customer Credential Exposure at Radware

Cybersecurity company Radware experienced a data breach after an unauthorized party accessed an unauthenticated internal Cloud WAF management API left reachable from the public internet on November 19, 2026.

🔍 Incident Overview

Radware detected the unauthorized access on a Thursday, ten hours after the initial intrusion. Upon detection, the company took several immediate response actions:

  • Blocked the originating IP address and disabled public access to the internal management API.
  • Revoked and replaced all internal account credentials.
  • Initiated a root cause analysis report, which was later shared by an anonymous source with BleepingComputer.

Founded in 1996 and headquartered in Tel Aviv, Radware provides application delivery and DDoS protection services to more than 12,500 enterprise and telecom carrier customers worldwide.

⚙️ Impacted Systems and Data

The exposure was limited to specific account management details and log export configurations, while core traffic inspection remained unaffected.

System / Data Category Status According to Radware
Customer contact details Potentially accessed
Log export credentials (AWS S3, Azure Blob Storage, SFTP) Potentially accessed for a subset of customers
WAF traffic inspection and certificates Not exposed
End-users’ data and customer application traffic Not exposed
Cloud DDoS services and data Not exposed

Radware stated that WAF traffic inspection and protection have continued without interruption, with no evidence found of policy changes or access to customer application traffic.

💡 Customer Action Advised

Radware strongly advised affected AppSec (WAF, BOT) customers to take immediate remedial steps:

  • Rotate exposed Cloud WAF log export credentials, including Azure Blob Storage keys or SAS tokens, AWS S3 access keys, or SFTP credentials, as soon as possible.
  • Review access logs on cloud storage accounts for unexpected access dating back to at least November 19.

The company noted it has already received reports from customers regarding AWS alerts for an unfamiliar IP address attempting to access their log-export buckets.

📊 Investigation and Public Response

Radware is continuing to investigate the incident to determine whether any exposed API keys or customer information were used without authorization. As of the report, Radware has not issued a public statement, filed a breach report with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, or provided an immediate response to inquiries from BleepingComputer.

#Cybersecurity #DataBreach #Radware #CloudSecurity #APISecurity

Source: Radware discloses breach exposing customer cloud access keys

item.title: Rackspace to Shut Down Spot Platform After Security Breach
item.description:
Rackspace to Shut Down Spot Platform After Security Breach

Rackspace is shutting down its Rackspace Spot cloud platform, which allows organizations to deploy and manage containerized applications using Kubernetes, following a security breach that allowed hackers to access customer clusters and secrets. Customers are given until December 8 to migrate their services and download their data before the platform is permanently discontinued.

🚨 The Breach and Discovery

The decision to discontinue the service comes after a security incident that occurred on November 17, when hackers breached Rackspace Spot using compromised credentials. The intrusion allowed unauthorized actors to create pods in customer Kubernetes clusters, read Kubernetes Secrets, and list nodes and volumes. Rackspace discovered the intrusion on November 18 following a customer report and subsequently disabled access to the platform’s administration console to secure its infrastructure.

The service was restored on November 21 following an extended outage. Rackspace stated that the affected Spot environment is segmented from its core infrastructure and that it has not identified evidence of unauthorized access to its core systems or the environments of other Rackspace customers.

⚙️ Customer Instructions and Indicators of Compromise

Rackspace has instructed all Spot customers to treat their API tokens, refresh tokens, kubeconfigs, and Kubernetes Secrets as potentially compromised, regardless of whether they previously received a breach notification. Customers are also advised to review access logs dating back to November 16 and search for suspicious Kubernetes objects associated with the attack.

The following indicators of compromise have been provided for customers to search within their logs:

Indicator Type Details
IP Address 23.224.79.106
IP Range 23.224.0.0/15
Suspicious Kubernetes Pod and Object Prefixes i1, glm-, and probe

📅 Shutdown Details

Rackspace announced the shutdown in a new security notification, stating it had decided to wind down the Rackspace Spot service to provide a clear path forward for customers. The service will be permanently discontinued on December 8, 2026, at 5 PM Central Time, at which point all remaining workloads will be terminated and customer data will no longer be accessible. Customers are instructed to retrieve their data and migrate their workloads to different platforms before this deadline.

💡 Customer Response

The shutdown announcement has prompted disappointment among Rackspace Spot customers, with some urging the company to reconsider and offering to pay more to keep the platform operational. In a Reddit discussion, one customer said they believed users would be willing to pay higher prices to keep the service running. Other customers expressed concerns about affordable alternatives and the impact the shutdown would have on their existing infrastructure, while others praised the service for its affordability. Rackspace has not indicated whether it will reconsider the shutdown decision or offer customers additional time to migrate their workloads.

#Rackspace #Security #Kubernetes #Cloud #DataBreach

Source: Rackspace shuts down Spot cloud platform after security breach

item.title: European Commission confirms data breach via AI-assisted attack
item.description:
European Commission confirms data breach via AI-assisted attack

The European Commission has confirmed that attackers breached its EU Academy online learning hub and stole the personal data of an undisclosed number of users. This incident follows a disclosure that hackers breached the Commission’s systems on October 22 using the ARTEX AI-powered penetration testing framework.

🔍 Overview

  • The attack was conducted using the ARTEX AI-powered penetration testing framework.
  • The breach affected the EU Academy platform, which is used to learn about EU policies and follow EU online courses.
  • The incident caused service disruptions that also affected the internal Sysper HR platform.
  • The Commission stated it has not detected evidence of a data breach affecting Commission staff as a whole.
  • No ransom demands have been received, and the attack has not yet been attributed to a specific actor.

🚨 Key details

  • Stolen data included users’ personal information, such as names and email addresses.
  • As a protective measure, the Commission temporarily took down several applications, most of which have since been restored.
  • Public access to the EU Academy platform has been disabled.
  • Users on the platform received a message warning them to be suspicious of unsolicited emails or messages that may be part of potential phishing attacks.
  • The investigation into the incident is still ongoing.

⚙️ Broader context

  • In February, the Commission disclosed a data breach after discovering on January 30 that a mobile device management platform used for staff devices had been compromised.
  • On March 27, the Commission disclosed an additional incident following a breach of its Amazon cloud environment.
  • The EU’s Cybersecurity Service (CERT-EU) attributed the March cloud hack to the TeamPCP threat group, noting it exposed the data of at least 29 other Union entities.
  • These incidents follow the Commission’s January 20 proposal for new cybersecurity legislation aimed at strengthening defenses against cybercrime groups and state-backed actors.

#EuropeanCommission #Cybersecurity #DataBreach #Artemis #AIHacking

Source: European Commission confirms data theft in EU Academy breach

item.title: KEPCO Data Breach Exposes 1.5 Million Individuals
item.description:
KEPCO Data Breach Exposes 1.5 Million Individuals

A threat actor breached the internal network of Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO), exposing details of more than 1.5 million individuals.

🔍 Overview

  • KEPCO, South Korea’s main electric power company, detected an attack on November 20.
  • The breach exposed customer, employee, and contractor data.
  • The attack was detected when unauthorized access was confirmed to KEPCO ON and SRM systems.

⚙️ Key details

  • The following data was exposed:
    • For 650,487 KEPCO ON customers: names, ID information, phone numbers, addresses, bank names, bank account numbers, account holder names, card issuers, card numbers, cardholder names, and electricity charge and billing information.
    • For 426,827 company representatives: names, ID information, email addresses, and company addresses.
    • For 442,934 KEPCO employees: names, affiliation, employee ID number, mobile phone number, email address, company phone number.
  • The data breach resulted from “advanced technologies as AI,” but specific details about the initial access method or attack chain were not shared.
  • KEPCO is notifying exposed individuals directly, has filed a report with the data protection authorities, and is coordinating with government and financial authorities to block abuse.

💡 Why it matters

  • Potentially exposed individuals are warned that the exposed information could be used for targeted phishing and impersonation.
  • They are advised to report any attempts to the police or Korea’s Internet and Security Agency.
  • It is recommended to avoid installing unknown apps, entering information into suspicious forms, and sharing sensitive data or verification codes over calls or texts.

🔗 Attribution

  • A threat actor using the “Noiem” alias has claimed the attack and advertised the breach on a hacker forum on November 19.
  • South Korea’s Personal Information Protection Commission separately confirmed that KEPCO received an email from a hacker claiming data theft on November 19.
  • While these claims match the available evidence, attribution to Noiem remains unconfirmed.

#KEPCO #DataBreach #CyberSecurity #SouthKorea #CriticalInfrastructure

Source: South Korea’s power giant KEPCO confirms data breach impacting 1.5 million

item.title: Cleverbridge Breach Exposes Customer Payment Card Data
item.description:
Cleverbridge Breach Exposes Customer Payment Card Data

Cleverbridge, an e-commerce platform that provides services to software and SaaS companies, disclosed that a security breach resulted in the theft of customers’ payment card information. The stolen data includes credit card numbers and CVV security codes.

🧩 Company Background

Cleverbridge enables software and SaaS companies to sell products, process payments, and manage subscriptions. The platform lists numerous technology brands among its customers, including:

  • Red Hat
  • SUSE
  • Tenable
  • Veeam
  • Jamf
  • Sony
  • Parallels

🔍 Incident Timeline

According to a security incident disclosure, the company detected unauthorized activity on November 4, 2026. Systems were temporarily taken offline to contain the breach and were brought back online the same day. The investigation subsequently determined that a third party copied payment card data stored on the platform.

Affected customers began receiving notifications on November 20, 2026.

⚙️ Data Stolen

A breach notification shared with BleepingComputer reveals that the stolen information includes:

  • Payment card numbers
  • Expiration dates
  • CVV/CVC security codes

The notification explicitly states that no other personal data, such as names, contact details, or billing information, were copied. The notice specifies that the affected card ends in a placeholder sequence.

🚫 What Was Not Involved

Cleverbridge confirmed that the incident was not a ransomware attack. Attackers did not encrypt any of the company’s systems. The company has not disclosed how the attackers gained access, how long they remained in the systems, or the total number of affected customers.

💡 Response and Remediation

Cleverbridge has notified data protection authorities, law enforcement, payment card networks, and payment partners regarding the incident. The company is working with TransUnion’s Cyberscout to distribute breach notifications and provide affected customers with complimentary credit monitoring and fraud assistance. Customers are advised to review their payment card statements for any unauthorized transactions.

#DataBreach #Cleverbridge #PaymentSecurity #Cybersecurity #CreditCardTheft

Source: Cleverbridge warns hackers stole credit card numbers, CVVs in data breach

item.title: Microsoft Suffers Data Breach Following Entra Connect Health Vulnerability
item.description:
Microsoft Suffers Data Breach Following Entra Connect Health Vulnerability

Microsoft is warning organizations that it suffered a data breach after attackers exploited a vulnerability in its Entra Connect Health service to gain unauthorized access to administrator email addresses and tenant configuration information.

🔍 Overview

  • Microsoft Entra Connect Health is a cloud-based monitoring service that allows administrators to monitor the health, performance, and alerts of their on-premises identity infrastructure through the Microsoft Entra admin center.
  • Microsoft discovered the vulnerability in the Entra Connect Health API on November 9, 2026, after it was first introduced on July 23.
  • An investigation determined that the flaw was exploited, allowing unauthorized parties to access tenant and service-monitoring metadata and potentially modify Connect Health monitoring configurations.
  • Microsoft concluded its investigation on November 20, 2026, determining that unauthorized read-only access to tenant-level metadata occurred, with no unauthorized configuration changes identified.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Email addresses belonging to tenant technical contacts and administrator accounts were exposed.
  • Tenant IDs, display names, initial domain names, country codes, and regional information were exposed.
  • Microsoft Entra license tiers and directory synchronization status, including whether synchronization was enabled and the last synchronization timestamp, were exposed.
  • Connect Health onboarding status was exposed.
  • An expired certificate previously used to register Connect Health agents with a Microsoft internal service that was decommissioned in late 2024 was exposed.
  • User passwords, password hashes, authentication tokens, valid cryptographic keys, on-premises server and Active Directory topology details, and Azure subscription information were not exposed.

🛠️ Timeline and Remediation

  • Microsoft deployed a server-side fix on November 19, 2026, to prevent further exploitation.
  • Microsoft finished its investigation on November 20 and began notifying affected organizations.
  • No software updates or other customer remediation are required to address the vulnerability.
  • Microsoft published a PowerShell script at https://aka.ms/ConnectHealth/scripts allowing administrators to view the types of tenant metadata that could have been exposed.

💡 Recommendations

  • Alert security teams to potential targeted phishing and social-engineering attacks targeting exposed administrator email addresses and tenant information.
  • Ensure privileged accounts use phishing-resistant multifactor authentication.
  • Review Connect Health configurations.
  • Examine Microsoft Entra audit and sign-in logs for suspicious activity.

#Microsoft #EntraConnectHealth #DataBreach #Cybersecurity

Source: Microsoft Entra Connect Health flaw exploited to steal tenant data

item.title: Rackspace Spot Breach Exposes Kubernetes Secrets and API Tokens
item.description:
Rackspace Spot Breach Exposes Kubernetes Secrets and API Tokens

Rackspace has warned customers that hackers breached its Rackspace Spot cloud platform using compromised credentials. The intrusion allowed unauthorized parties to deploy workloads and access sensitive Kubernetes secrets within customer clusters.

🔍 Overview

Rackspace disclosed the breach in a notification to affected customers, stating that attackers accessed parts of the platform on November 17, 2026, between approximately 00:20 and 22:00 UTC. The company learned of the intrusion on November 18 after receiving a customer report and confirmed that the recipient’s organization was affected that same day.

⚙️ Key details

  • Access Method: An unauthorized party used leaked credentials to act as legitimate users in some customer organizations.
  • Actions Taken: Attackers created pods in Kubernetes clusters, read Kubernetes Secrets, and listed nodes and volumes.
  • Exposure Risk: Attackers could have read any Secret stored in an affected user’s clusters, as well as any Spot API tokens or refresh tokens held by that user.
  • Indicators: The breach was associated with IP address 23.224.79.106, IP range 23.224.0.0/15, and suspicious Kubernetes pod and object prefixes including i1, glm-, and probe.

🛡️ Remediation and Response

Rackspace stated that it has revoked affected tokens and sessions, removed the unauthorized pods, rotated keys, and strengthened access controls and monitoring. Affected customers were instructed to:

  • Reissue their Spot API tokens.
  • Replace refresh tokens used in automation tools.
  • Download fresh Kubernetes configuration files.
  • Rotate credentials stored in their cluster Secrets.
  • Analyze logs associated with databases, container registries, Git repositories, cloud storage, and third-party services dating back to November 17 to identify possible abuse of exposed credentials.

The breach caused an extended outage of the Rackspace Spot administration console, temporarily preventing customers from managing their clusters or rotating credentials. Sirish Raghuram, co-founder and Chief Growth Officer of Platform9, explained that the team deliberately disabled access while securing its infrastructure. Rackspace announced that service was fully restored on November 21.

#Rackspace #Kubernetes #CloudSecurity #DataBreach

Source: Rackspace Spot breach let hackers access customer Kubernetes secrets

item.title: Bell Canada Investigates Data Breach Linked to Agentic Threat Actor
item.description:
Bell Canada Investigates Data Breach Linked to Agentic Threat Actor

Bell Canada has confirmed that an “agentic” threat actor breached its systems on November 17, 2026, and stole enterprise customer data. The unauthorized access targeted multiple systems, including a pre-production environment of the company’s Maximo system, which is used to order and provision telecommunications network connections and circuits.

#Cybersecurity #AIAgents #DataBreach

item.title: FBI Investigates Second Reported System Breach in Two Months
item.description:
FBI Investigates Second Reported System Breach in Two Months

FBI systems have reportedly been breached for the second time in two months, this time targeting the agency’s National Crime Information Center (NCIC). The NCIC is used to share information between local, state, and federal law enforcement agencies.

🔍 Overview

  • The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of the NCIC system, according to CNN’s reporting citing two people briefed on the investigation.
  • The intrusion was reportedly discovered in recent days.
  • It is unclear when the breach occurred, how the attackers gained access, or whether any information was stolen.
  • The FBI has not publicly confirmed the incident and did not respond to CNN’s request for comment.
  • BleepingComputer contacted the FBI on Friday evening with questions about the reported breach but has not received a response.
  • This is a developing story and will be updated as more information becomes available.

⚙️ Key details

  • The National Crime Information Center is an FBI-operated database used across the United States to share information about wanted and missing persons, outstanding arrest warrants, stolen vehicles and firearms, protection orders, and other criminal justice records.
  • Police officers routinely use the system during traffic stops, criminal investigations, and background checks.
  • It remains unclear whether attackers accessed sensitive law enforcement records stored in NCIC or whether the intrusion affected system availability.

🧩 Context and Prior Incidents

  • The reported breach comes two months after the ShinyHunters extortion group claimed to have breached FBI systems by exploiting an unpatched Oracle PeopleSoft vulnerability.
  • The earlier attack targeted a third-party platform associated with the FBI’s recruitment website, FBIJobs.gov, with ShinyHunters claiming to have stolen sensitive information.
  • The FBI subsequently launched an investigation leading to the arrests of suspected ShinyHunters members, including a Canadian cybersecurity executive reportedly linked to the attacks.
  • There is currently no indication that the latest NCIC incident is connected to ShinyHunters or the earlier breach.

#FBI #Cybersecurity #DataBreach #NCIC #LawEnforcement

Source: FBI reportedly hacked again, this time targeting nationwide police database

item.title: JPMorgan Chase Warns of Data Breach via Third-Party Cyberattack
item.description:
JPMorgan Chase Warns of Data Breach via Third-Party Cyberattack

J.P. Morgan Chase announced that it suffered a data breach following a cyberattack on a third-party service provider, which exposed customers’ personal information and marketing data. The bank stated that its services were not disrupted and the incident is unrelated to a service disruption that occurred earlier in the week.

🏦 Banking Sector Impact

J.P. Morgan Chase Bank is the largest U.S. bank by assets, with about $4.1 trillion as of June 2026, and its consumer banking division reports about 78 million active digital customers. The bank’s announcement on X stated, “We have learned that third parties who provide services to the firm were the target of a cyber attack.” The bank further disclosed, “Based on our investigation so far, we believe the attackers accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors, which may include some customer names and email addresses.”

💳 Payment Networks Affected

Visa and Mastercard confirmed that they were involved in third-party incidents, though both have not confirmed any impact on customers or their core payment networks.

  • Visa: A spokesperson told BleepingComputer that the incident is “associated with an incident involving a third-party service provider in Asia Pacific.” Visa stated, “Visa’s systems were not involved and were not impacted. No payments data such as card numbers were affected.”
  • Mastercard: The company confirmed it was “informed of an incident at a third-party provider that resulted in the exposure of limited amount of email addresses – non-payments information – from a small subset of cardholders enrolled in a specific benefit program.” A spokesperson assured that “There is no impact to the Mastercard payment network or the ability for people to use their cards.”

🏭 Third-Party Provider

On November 11, 2026, the n0n ransomware group claimed responsibility for an attack on Qubole, a cloud data analytics company owned by Idera, suspected to be the third-party provider used by the financial institutions. Qubole is used for cloud data analytics, automated processing, real-time analysis, and reporting.

📊 Stolen Data and Extortion

Between October 14 and 26, 2026, the n0n ransomware group allegedly used compromised Qubole credentials to access customers’ AWS environments through IAM roles configured to grant Qubole access. The group claimed to have stolen 53.9 GB across 30,743 files directly from Qubole, including customer contracts, pricing records, staff and trial-user information, and production data. Additionally, they claimed to hold nearly one petabyte of data from Qubole’s customer networks. The n0n group leaked the claimed data on its extortion site on November 16, 2026, stating that their extortion demands were ignored after contacting Qubole and the affected companies.

#JPMorganChase #Ransomware #Cybersecurity #Qubole #DataBreach #VisaMastercard

item.title: NVIDIA Investigates Third-Party Partner Incident Following Gentlemen Ransomware Claims
item.description:
NVIDIA Investigates Third-Party Partner Incident Following Gentlemen Ransomware Claims

NVIDIA is investigating claims of a security breach after the Gentlemen ransomware group added the company to its dark web data leak site, though no proof of the breach has been shared yet.

🔍 Overview

  • The Gentlemen ransomware group listed NVIDIA on its dark web data leak site and threatened to release data with a countdown ending in nine days on November 28.
  • NVIDIA stated it has not found evidence that its systems were compromised, but is looking into a separate incident that may have affected a third-party partner.
  • An NVIDIA spokesperson told BleepingComputer: “We have found no indication that NVIDIA systems or networks were affected. We continue to monitor the situation.”

⚙️ Key details

  • The Gentlemen surfaced last year as a closed ransomware group before switching to a Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) model.
  • The group offers affiliates up to a 90% cut of ransom proceeds.
  • It operates as a double-extortion group that exfiltrates sensitive data before encrypting systems and threatening to leak the information.
  • Since emerging, The Gentlemen has claimed more than 1,100 victims across manufacturing, healthcare, transportation, energy, education, and financial services sectors.

#NVIDIA #Ransomware #Cybersecurity #DataBreach

Source: NVIDIA investigating Gentlemen ransomware breach claims

item.title: SBC Medical Group Exposes Data of 1.6 Million Individuals
item.description:
SBC Medical Group Exposes Data of 1.6 Million Individuals

SBC Medical Group disclosed in a U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filing that two separate cybersecurity incidents resulted in the unauthorized exposure of sensitive customer and employee information, affecting a total of 1.6 million people.

⚠️ The Breach

The company, a clinic management firm primarily operating in Japan with a limited U.S. presence and Nasdaq listing (SBC), revealed that the incidents impacted its Japan-based businesses. The breach was identified on November 16, 2026, when unauthorized access occurred to certain databases within a website system managed by the company’s Japanese subsidiary.

The data affected by this database incident included:

  • Basic personal information belonging to 1,624,000 people.
  • 255,416 reservation requests.
  • 217,769 inquiries submitted to SBC websites.
  • Thousands of treatment description records, image filenames, and customer reviews.
  • Approximately 20,000 employee account records containing names, IDs, and passwords.
  • Bank account and tax information for a subset of 459 employees.

🏥 The Tribeau Compromise

Simultaneously on November 16, SBC was notified of a second incident involving unauthorized access to clinic administrator accounts on Tribeau, a third-party booking platform. This breach affected reservation information for 12,641 people and accessed treatment names, dates, and fees for 6,804 patients who received treatment at 56 clinics using the service.

📊 Current Status

SBC confirmed that the attackers extracted customer information but stated that they have not confirmed unauthorized access to electronic medical records or information from the mySBC reservation site. The method of intrusion and full scope remain under investigation. As of the November 18 filing, the company had not seen evidence of misuse of the exposed data and could not estimate the financial impact of the incidents.

#SBCMedical #DataBreach #Cybersecurity #SECFiling #HealthcareSecurity

Source: Hackers steal data of 1.6 million SBC Medical Group customers

item.title: TfL data breach impacts 265,000 Oyster photocard customers
item.description:
TfL data breach impacts 265,000 Oyster photocard customers

Transport for London (TfL) announced that approximately 265,000 Oyster photocard customers may have had their account details exposed in a security incident discovered on November 16, 2026. The breach was identified after customers reported receiving emails from TfL’s mail systems requesting them to create an account.

🔍 Overview

TfL operates London’s public transport network, including the Underground, Overground, buses, trams, and the Elizabeth line, recording 3.53 billion passenger journeys in 2025/26. The Oyster photocard website has been taken offline, and data breach notifications are being sent to impacted individuals. The incident has been contained, and TfL has notified the UK’s Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO).

⚙️ Key Details

The data leak involved the following personal information:

  • Full names
  • Phone numbers
  • Email addresses
  • Home addresses
  • Dates of birth
  • Security questions and answers

TfL’s assessment indicates that passwords, bank and payment card details, journey information, and the names and dates of birth of children with Zip Oyster cards were not compromised. No evidence of misuse has been found so far.

💡 Why It Matters

The exposure of security questions and answers is particularly concerning because these details may be used for account access restoration. Customers who received the suspicious email should ignore it and remain vigilant for further activity. Once the Oyster photocard portal is restored, all photocard customers will be prompted to change their password, security question, and answer.

Recommendation Detail
Account Security Change passwords, security questions, and answers on Oyster photocard
Cross-Site Security Rotate security questions used at other sites
General Hygiene Change passwords on other services where the same information was used
Reporting Report suspicious activity to TfL Customer Services immediately

Oyster photocards remain valid for travel. Customers who need to renew their cards or check journey history can contact TfL’s Customer Services.

#DataBreach #TransportForLondon #OysterPhotocard #CyberSecurity #UK

Source: Transport for London breach exposes 265,000 Oyster card users’ data

item.title: Why Password Spreadsheets Fail to Capture Employee Credential Behavior
item.description:
Why Password Spreadsheets Fail to Capture Employee Credential Behavior

Password spreadsheets used by administrators often present a false sense of completeness, as they only reflect credentials that employees have explicitly reported, missing passwords that have been changed, created, or shared since the last update.

🔍 The Visibility Gap

Administrators may believe they have a handle on company credentials, but this view is incomplete unless someone actively updates the document. Work passwords frequently end up in untracked locations, including:

  • Browser built-in storage
  • Shared Google documents or chat messages (e.g., Slack)
  • Personal vaults used because official access is too slow
  • Sticky notes on desks

⚙️ Drivers of Unreported Use

The predominant factor in this behavior is convenience. When approved processes are slow or unclear, employees prioritize getting work done by using tools immediately at hand, even if they know it violates rules. Because employees rarely manually report every new password, update, or shared credential, these spreadsheets fail to capture the actual state of credential usage.

📊 Credential Weakness and Reuse

Lack of visibility prevents companies from knowing if critical assets are protected by weak passwords. Evidence highlights significant risks:

  • Reuse: Verizon’s 2025 Data Breach Investigations Report found that in the median case, only 49% of users’ passwords were unique, meaning more than half were reused across services.
  • Weakness: The ‘TOP 20 Not-So-Secret Business Passwords’ report by NordPass identified ‘123456’ as the most common corporate password.
  • Complexity: Verizon’s report found that only 3% of compromised passwords in its dataset met basic complexity standards.

Without visibility into storage locations, admins cannot determine who uses a password, who it has been shared with, or if it has been changed. Consequently, they cannot assess the strength or reuse of daily credentials.

⚠️ Security Implications

If attackers gain access to a password spreadsheet, they may encrypt it for ransom or use the credentials inside to access other systems, spreading the attack further. The 2026 edition of the Verizon Data Breach Investigations Report identified credential abuse as the initial access vector in 13% of breaches, while vulnerability exploitation accounted for 31%, underscoring the need for integrated credential protection.

To keep accounts protected, admins need to answer specific questions about each password: Is it strong? Who owns it? Where is it stored? Who has access? Is it reused, old, or exposed in a breach? Strong passwords are still at risk if reused across accounts, as exposure in one breach can lead to access to others.

💡 Mitigation Features

Tools like NordPass allow administrators to set password requirements to ensure strength and enable users to share credentials over protected channels. Key features include:

  • Sharing Hub: Displays who has access to passwords shared with multiple people or teams.
  • Activity Log: Records actions related to company passwords.

#PasswordManagement #Cybersecurity #CredentialSecurity #DataBreach

Source: Still tracking company passwords in spreadsheets? You’re flying blind.

item.title: AI-Powered Automation Inverts Cyber Kill Chain Leading to Large Scale Tech Breaches
item.description:
AI-Powered Automation Inverts Cyber Kill Chain Leading to Large Scale Tech Breaches

The technology industry is currently experiencing a period of continuous security breaches, characterized by the automation of the traditional cyber kill chain through AI. According to Alex Stamos, chief security officer at Cognition and lecturer at the Stanford University Cyber Policy Center, AI-enabled systems are now capable of finding vulnerabilities and writing exploits in real time, shifting these activities from a long-term research phase to immediate execution.

🧩 How it works

The traditional cyber kill chain involves upfront research, finding vulnerabilities, and writing exploits well before an attack occurs. AI has inverted this process through the following capabilities:

  • AI systems autonomously scan targets for bugs in real time.
  • The systems identify vulnerabilities and write functional exploits immediately.
  • Open-weight models have reached a level of sophistication that allows for the automation of most of the kill chain.

⚙️ Key details

Recent events illustrate how these automated attacks are being chained together across the tech industry, affecting neoclouds and AI-related companies:

Incident or Tool Description
Binance Hack Described as the largest heist of anything in human history.
Fireworks A prominent AI service provider that was breached; stolen API keys were used to access other systems.
Cursor Incident Attackers used stolen keys to push a bad plugin to 5,000 companies, resulting in 5,000 potential breaches.
ARTEX A Chinese open-source tool, available with an English translation on GitHub, used to automate attacks.
Obliterated GLM-5.3 A specific model that can power tools like ARTEX to break into a large number of organizations.

💡 Why it matters

Alex Stamos suggests that the multibillion-dollar cybersecurity industry is overdue for disruption as AI-boosted attacks increase. State actors, including Russia and North Korea, are currently utilizing AI to detect and exploit vulnerabilities simultaneously. While Stamos is not a long-term doomer, he indicates that the industry is entering a dark age as it struggles to adapt to these new adversary capabilities and the resulting waves of hacks.

#Cybersecurity #ArtificialIntelligence #DataBreach

Source: How AI broke cybersecurity

item.title: Security Breach Exposes Millions of Private Conversations from Eiliko Robot Toys
item.description:
Security Breach Exposes Millions of Private Conversations from Eiliko Robot Toys

Energize Lab’s “Eiliko” digital pet robot has been found to have severe security vulnerabilities that expose private user data and conversations. While the AI companion tells users their secrets are safe, researchers discovered that the company stores millions of unprotected transcripts, personal profiles, and unencrypted photos on Chinese servers accessible to hackers.

🔍 Overview

Eiliko is a marshmallow-shaped robot designed to change its cartoony expressions to match a user’s mood. However, conversations held over Wi-Fi are transmitted to servers in China where they are stored in a completely unprotected state. Researcher Azdoufal found that the service’s lack of security allowed access to 13 million conversations and the entire active worldwide fleet of 68,000 robot toys.

Data Category Details and Findings
User Profiles Includes name, age, birthday, profession, family, friends, and personality assessments.
Technical Data Emails, IP addresses, and searchable full-text databases of all user conversations.
Media Storage Unencrypted photos of children and short audio recordings stored at public web addresses.
Fleet Scale 68,000 active robots, with over 31,000 profiles belonging to children in the United States.

⚙️ Key Details

  • AI Profiling: The service analyzes conversations to create psychological profiles. One log described a 52-year-old user as someone who “values friendship” but “has difficulty trusting family members.”
  • Vulnerability Reports: Nine official CVE vulnerability reports are being published by Azdoufal and Tod Beardsley regarding Energize Lab’s security failures.
  • Security Practices: Many admin passwords used by the company were found on “most common passwords” lists.
  • Corporate Response: Energize Lab has not addressed the breach effectively, providing only robotic automated replies to repeated inquiries from researchers and journalists.

💡 Why it matters

Beyond data theft, the robot’s memory and Large Language Model (LLM) can be remotely hijacked. During testing, a researcher from across the globe successfully changed a toy’s personality and memory. The hijacked robot began telling the user they had a different name, claimed their parents had died in an accident, and stated that the Earth is flat. While the LLM maintains some basic guardrails—such as warning against getting into a stranger’s car—the ability to bypass its intended personality poses significant risks to users.

#Cybersecurity #Privacy #Robotics #DataBreach

Source: Your secrets aren’t safe with this cute robot toy — they’re on Chinese servers ready to be hacked
